newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ABR leaps 34 pct in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: ABR leaps 34 pct in speculative trade.

text.p: ABR Holdings shares jumped more than 34 percent on Thursday to hit a high of Singapore $1.55 in speculative trading, dealers said.
At 0846 GMT, the stock had eased to S$1.51, up 38 cents with more than 6.9 million shares changing hands.
Dealers said there were all sorts of rumours in the market about ABR, which is controlled by Indonesian businessman Johannes Kotjo.
"We noticed all the Kotjo counters started moving in the afternoon," said one broker.
Kotjo also controls Van der Horst, which was up 22 cents to S$2.64, and L&M Group Investments, up 13 cents to S$1.47.
"I heard syndicates were going to move ABR this morning," said another dealer.
Dealers said there were various rumours that Kotjo was going to sell out of ABR and L&M to other Indonesian parties and subsequently inject funds to support Van der Horst.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment on the rumour.
